## Philosophy quotes about inquiry

Inquiry is the disciplined pursuit of better questions and answers—philosophy as method rather than dogma.

17 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

### Why this theme matters

Socratic elenchus, scientific method, and pragmatist experimentalism treat inquiry as self-correcting. The ethics of inquiry asks for intellectual honesty.

### In the history of philosophy

Academies, laboratories, and public debate inherit ideals of inquiry that philosophy both practices and criticizes.

[Aristotle](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/aristotle) , [Heraclitus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/heraclitus) , [Anselm of Canterbury](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/anselm-of-canterbury) , [Michel de Montaigne](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/michel-de-montaigne) , [Plutarch](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plutarch) , [Confucius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/confucius) , [The Doctrine of the Mean](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-doctrine-of-the-mean) , [Francis Bacon](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/francis-bacon)

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is inquiry in philosophy?

It is the process of investigating questions with reasons, evidence, and willingness to revise belief.

#### How does philosophical inquiry differ from science?

It often targets conceptual and normative questions science presupposes, while remaining continuous with scientific curiosity.

#### Where are philosophy quotes about inquiry?

This theme collects passages on questioning, wonder, and the examined life.
